text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"Periodically consolidating appended knowledge into a compressed summary (as described in the consolidation vs accumulation and consolidation reduces interference papers) will alleviate the capacity‑interference drop observed after ~40 items in the append‑only QA experiment, restoring or improving accuracy beyond that point.","confidence":0.78,"support_ids":["e8af7ee8","085f93d4","45562236","d421fc37"],"tags":["capacity","consolidation","interference"]},{"statement":"Integrating a virtual‑context paging system similar to MemGPT into the memory architecture can provide a middle ground between naive append and full rewrite, allowing older items to be paged out and rewritten on demand; this hybrid approach should achieve the performance gains attributed to rewrite operations while satisfying the reviewer’s demand for an ablation that isolates the effect of rewrite versus mere memory presence.","confidence":0.66,"support_ids":["800e430c","d421fc37","853b30eb"],"tags":["paging","ablation","rewrite"]}]}
